title: 2007 Which Was Sent On 04.10.2007 By Way ... vs State on 7 June, 2012
full_text: 2007 Which Was Sent On 04.10.2007 By Way ... vs State on 7 June, 2012 CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 1 of Pages 21 IN THE COURT OF SH. GAJENDER SINGH NAGAR METROPOLITAN MAGISTRATE, KKD, EAST, NEW DELHI Complaint No. 6944/10 Unique ID No. 02402R0736872007 PS. Preet Vihar Sh. Anil Kumar Jain, S/o Sh. Ram Kumar Jain, 206, Second Floor, 10, Sikka Complex, Commercial Complex, Preet Vihar, Delhi­92 ......... Complainant. Versus 1. M/s B.T. Distributors Pvt Ltd 2. Sh. Umesh Wahi, Director of M/s B.T. Distributors Pvt Ltd S/o Late Sh. J.N. Wahi A­205, Jaipuria, Indrapuram Ghaziabad (U.P.). 3. Pooja Wahi, W/o Sh. Umesh Wahi A­205, Jaipuria, Indrapuram Ghaziabad (U.P.). ......... Accused. COMPLAINT U/s 138 OF THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT Offence complained of : U/s 138 N.I. Act Date of commission of offence : 21.10.2007 Plea of Accused : Not guilty Complaint filed on : 14.11.2007 Final Arguments heard & Concluded on : 22.05.2012 Date of decision of the case : 07.06.2012 Final order : Conviction of accused no. 1 & 2 Acquittal of accused no. 3 CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 2 of Pages 21 BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE CASE 1. By way of the present judgment, this court shall decide the complaint case U/s 138 Negotiable Instrument Act 1881 (as amended up to date) filed by the complainant Sh. Anil Kumar Jain against the accused B.T. Distributors Pvt Ltd & Others. 2. The facts in brief necessary for the disposal of the present case are that accused no.1 is a company and accused no.2 & 3 are its directors. The complainant and accused no.2 & 3 had entered into an agreement to sell dated 11.07.2007, for sale of one flat bearing no.33 SF, Jaipuria Apartment, Kaushambi, Ghaziabad (U.P.) and the complainant made an advance payment of Rs.3,50,000/­(three lacs fifty thousand) to the accused persons as a token money for that transaction. It was also agreed between the parties that the sale transaction will be completed by 31.08.2007. That on 30.08.2007, accused no. 2 & 3 requested the complainant for extension of the time for a further period i.e. till 25.09.2007 and also requested for some more advance payment, complainant accepted and acceded to it, by making a second advance payment of Rs.2,30,000/­(rupees two lacs thirty thousand only) to the accused no.2 & 3 on 30.08.2007 and then the date for execution of sale deed and balance payment of sale consideration of Rs. 19,20,000/­ has been fixed for 25.09.2007. However the accused no. 2 & 3 before the transaction date i.e. 25.09.2007 sold the above said flat to some other party and failed to perform their contract / obligation and failed to deliver the above mentioned flat to the complainant even after receiving a token money of Rs.5,80,000/­ (Five lacs eighty thousand). Being failed to perform their contract the accused persons offered a payment of Rs.6,00,000/­(six lacs) to the complainant Rs.5,80,000/­ as principal amount and Rs. 20,000/­ (twenty thousand) as interest and compensation for the non performance. Consequently the accused persons issued a cheque bearing no 998747 dated 21.09.2007 for the sum of Rs. CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 3 of Pages 21 6,00,000/­ drawn on Syndicate Bank, G­S­4, Scope Minar complex, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi­92 in favour of the complainant but on presentation the said cheque was returned back dishonored with the remark "INSUFFICIENT FUND" vide dishonour memo dated 21.09.2007. Thereafter a legal notice was sent to the accused on 01.10.2007 which was sent on 04.10.2007 by way of regd AD and UPC. It is further alleged that despite service of legal notice accused has not paid any thing to the complainant till the filling of the case. 3. After the complaint was filed, the complainant led the pre­ summoning evidence by way of an affidavit and after hearing the counsel for the complainant and considering the entire material and documents on record, summons were issued against the accused vide order dated 14.11.2007 for the offence U/s 138 Negotiable Instrument Act 1881. On appearance of the accused a separate notice U/s 251 Cr.P.C . dated 20.09.2008 was framed upon the accused persons to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 4. In order to prove the case, the complainant examined himself as CW­1 and reiterated the contents of the complaint on oath before this court and filed an affidavit in evidence. He also exhibited Agreement to sell as Ex. CW1/A, original cheque bearing No. 998747 as Ex. CW1/B, the cheque returning memo is Ex. CW1/C, the legal notice of demand dated 01.10.2007 is exhibited as Ex. CW1/D1, The original receipts of registered post are Ex. CW1/D2 to Ex. CW1/D4, U.P.C. is Ex. CW1/D5, registered AD are Ex. CW1/D6 & Ex. CW1/D7. He also examined Mr. D.K. Arora, Manager Syndicate Bank, Nirman Vihar brach (i.e. the bank of the complainant) as CW­2 who exhibited the certified copy of Account statement of the complainant as Ex. CW2/A, Mr. S.K. Vimal, Manager, Syndicate Bank, Nirman Vihar branch as CW­3 who exhibited the Log record CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 4 of Pages 21 as Ex. CW3/DA, Mr. Anil Kumar Aggarwal Senior Branch Manager, Syndiate Bank, Scope Minar branch, Laxmi Nagar as CW­4 who exhibited the statement of account of M/s B.T. Distributors Pvt Ltd as Ex. CW4/A, Mr. Rajiv Jain, Deputy Manager, Syndicate Bank, Scope Minar, Laxmi Nagar branch as CW­5 who exhibited the Time log record of M/s B.T. Distributors Pvt Ltd as Ex. CW5/1, the complainant also examined Mr. R.C. Laloria, Branch Manager, Syndicate Bank, Vikas Marg, Delhi­92 as CW­6. Thereafter, the complainant evidence was closed at request. 5. After that on 15.10.2011 the statements of accused persons were recorded U/s 313 Cr.P.C in which all the incriminating evidence along with exhibited documents were put to the accused persons. In their statement accused persons stated that they have never entered into any agreement to sell with the complainant thus there was no question of completing the sale transaction. It is further stated by the accused persons that they never issued the cheque in question to the complainant rather the same was handed over by accused no. 2 to their Chartered Accountant Mr. Raghvender for taxation purpose in blank signed condition. In their statement it is submitted by both the accused persons that they never received any legal notice sent by the complainant. Thereafter the case was fixed for Defence evidence, however no witness was examined by the accused persons in their defence and Defence Evidence was closed at the request of Ld. Defence Counsel and the matter was fixed for final arguments. 6. I have heard Ld. counsels and perused the entire record of the case file and the evidence on record. Both the counsel have referred to a number of cases, I have discussed them at the relevant place. 7. Before proceeding further let us go through the relevant provisions of law. The main ingredient of Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act are as follows:­ CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 5 of Pages 21 (a) The accused issued a cheque on an account maintained by him with a bank. (b) The said cheque has been issued in discharge of any legal debt or other liability. (c) The cheque has been presented to the bank within the period of six months from the date of the cheque or within the period of its validity. (d) When the aforesaid cheque was presented for encashment, the same was returned unpaid/ dishonoured. (e) The Payee of the cheque issued a legal notice of demand within 30 days from the receipt of information by him from the Bank regarding the return of the cheque. (f) The Drawer of the cheque failed to make the payment within 15 days of the receipt of the aforesaid legal notice of demand. If the aforesaid ingredients are satisfied then the drawer of the cheque shall be deemed to have committed an offence punishable u/s 138 Negotiable Instruments Act . If the aforesaid ingredients are satisfied then the drawer of the cheque shall be deemed to have committed an offence punishable u/s 138 Negotiable Instruments Act . 8. In the present matter a number of defences have been raised by the Ld. Defence Counsel which are as follows: i) That no legal notice was issued to the accused no.1 B.T. Distributors or to the accused no.3 Pooja Wahi. It is further submitted by him that notice issued to accused Umesh Wahi referring him as Managing Director of Accused no. 1 B.T. Distributors is not in itself deemed to be a proper notice on accused no.1 B.T. Distributors. ii) That accused no. 1 B.T. Distributors is not liable to make payment in respect of the cheque in question as the cheque was allegedly issued to return the amount received by accused no. 2 & 3 under an agreement to sell entered into by CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 6 of Pages 21 them in their individual capacity. Further, since the case has been filed against B.T. Distributors and accused no. 2 & 3 have been made by vicariously liable, but accused no.3 Pooja Wahi is not proved to be responsible for managing the day to day affairs of the accused no.1, hence, she deserves to be acquitted. iii) The notice U/s 251 Cr. PC was not duly framed as it was not signed by the Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate. Further though the cheque number and other details in the notice are correct but the name of the complainant is not correct as name of the present complainant is Anil Kumar Jain while in notice name of the complainant is written as Sanjeev Kumar. It is also argued by Ld. Defence Counsel that this legal notice was not framed on accused no.1 B.T. Distributors, hence, they are liable to be acquitted. Let the defences of the accused persons be decided first, Ld. Defence Counsel have relied on a case decided by Hon'ble High Court of Madras Citation 2006 Law Suit (Mad) 1827 titled as B. Raman, B. Ramesh & B. Raghu v. Shashunt Chemicals & Drugs , wherein it was held that when the offence is committed by a company, by virtue of Section 141 NI Act, every person, who at the time offence committed, was In­charge of and responsible for conduct of the business of the company, is presumed to be guilty of the offence. Thus the word "drawer", as contained in Section 138 (b) NI Act can not be restricted to the drawer of the cheque only, and will include all the persons who are liable to be prosecuted by virtue of Section 141 NI Act. Hence, separate statutory notice is required to be issued to every person / Director who is sought to be prosecuted by virtue of Section 141 NI Act is mandatory. In the present matter it is admitted by the Counsel for the complainant that they had sent only one notice which was addressed to Umesh Wahi, Director of M/s B.T. Distributors and no separate notice was CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 7 of Pages 21 sent to accused Pooja Wahi or to M/s B.T. Distributors. However it is argued by the Ld. Counsel for the complainant that this single notice is sufficient to be considered as notice to the accused no.1 M/s B.T. Distributors and when the notice is deemed to be served on accused no. 1 M/s B.T. Distributors then there is no need to give a separate notice to the accused Pooja Wahi who is also one of the directors of accused no. 1 M/s B.T. Distributors and is also the wife of accused no.2. I have heard both the parties on this defence as per the law laid down by Hon'ble Madras High Court a separate notice was required to be served upon accused Pooja Wahi, which was not served, hence, she has been acquitted from the present case on this short issue itself as serving a legal notice is sina qua non for the offence Under Section 138 NI Act. However the notice sent to accused Umesh Wahi referred as Director of M/s B.T. Distributors and sent to the offices of M/s B.T. Distributors will amount to a proper notice U/s 138 NI Act upon M/s B.T. Distributors and accused Umesh Wahi who has accepted that he is the managing director of M/s B.T. Distributors. Further accused Umesh Wahi is the signatory of the cheque, who signed the same as Director of M/s B.T. Distributors and he has also been called as accused in the present matter, hence there is no infirmity in notice issued U/s 138 NI Act (Relying on the Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, Bilak Chand Gyan chand Company v. A. Chinnaswami , 199(9) Supreme 469.). The second defence raised by the Ld. Defence Counsel is that the accused no. 1 M/s B.T. Distributors can not be held liable for making the payment in respect of the cheque in question as the cheque in question was issued to repay an alleged liability incurred by the directors of M/s B.T. Distributors in their personal capacity and M/s B.T. Distributors had no transactions with the CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 8 of Pages 21 complainant. Ld. Counsel for the complainant argued otherwise on the basis of a case decided by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anil Sacchar v. Shree Nath Spinners 2011(3) Crimes 142 S.C. I have heard both the parties, as per Indian Contract Act , a promise is enforceable if there is some consideration for it and it is quite immaterial whether it moves from the promise or any other person as held in Chinnayya Vs. Rammayya (1882) 4 Mad 137. Similarly in a number of cases it was held that words 'any debt or liability' in Section 138 NI Act would include a cheque drawn by one person towards legally enforceable debt or liability of another as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anil Sacchar v. Shree Nath Spinners 2011(3) Crimes 142 S.C , in that case cheques were issued by one sister concern towards liability of other sister concern. Similarly Hon'ble High Court of Delhi also in case Pratap Singh Yadav v. Atal Bihari Pandey 2003 (2) Crimes 343, held that where the cheque is issued by son for discharging debt of his father, then only the son shall be liable for offence and father cannot be prosecuted. On the basis of above stated discussion it is hereby held that accused B.T. Distributors can be held liable U/s 138 NI Act for the cheque issued towards payment of alleged personal liability of its directors. The other defence raised by the Ld. Defene Counsel is that notice U/s 251 Cr. PC is faulty as it does not bear the signature of Ld. Presiding Officer, no notice was given to accused M/s B.T. Distributors and name of the complainant is not correct in the notice. I have heard both the parties on this defence. It is a settled principal of law, when the prosecution witnesses were cross examined at length and accused has been adequately examined U/s 313 Cr. PC, then non compliance of Section 251 Cr. PC does not vitiate the trial. In the present case the accused examined the complainant witnesses in details and the accused persons have not been prejudiced because certain faults in the notice U/s 251 Cr. CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 9 of Pages 21 PC. Further accused Umesh Wahi is the managing director of accused M/s B.T. Distributors hence, the notice is also deemed to be given to the accused M/s B.T. Distributors. 9. WHETHER THE CHEQUE WAS ISSUED OR NOT: CW1 has stated in his examine in chief that cheque in question was issued by the accused persons. In their examination U/s 315 Cr. PC it was submitted by the accused persons that they never issued the cheque in question to the complainant. It was further submitted by accused no. 2 Umesh Wahi that the cheque in question was handed over by him in blank signed condition to their Chartered Accountant Mr. Raghvender for taxation purpose, However the accused persons failed to produce any cogent evidence to prove the same as Mr. Raghvender was not produced as defence witness. Thus the contention of the accused that the cheque was given to Mr. Raghvender is not proved. Further the legal position in respect to the blank signed cheques is as under: In Jaipal Singh Rana Vs. Swaraj Pal 149 (2008) DLT 682 it was held by Delhi High Court that "by putting the amount and the name of payee there is no material alteration on the cheque U/s 87 of the Negotiable Instruments Act . In fact there is no alteration but only adding the amount and the date. It was further observed in the aforesaid judgment that there is no rule of banking business that the name of the payee as well as the amount should be written by the drawer himself. No law provides that in case of cheques the entire body has to be written by the drawer only. " In Ravi Chopra v. State & another (2008 (2) LRC 118 del) it was held by the Hon'ble high court that "it is possible for drawer of a cheque to give a blank cheque signed by him to the payee and consent either impliedly or expressly to the said cheque being filed by the payee at a subsequent point of time". CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 10 of Pages 21 Similarly it was held by the Kerala High Court in lillykutty v. lawrence (2004 (1) JCC (NI) 14), that there is no rule in banking business that payee's name and the amount should be written by drawer himself. Further the burden is on the accused to establish that the date, amount and payee's name are written by somebody else without the knowledge and consent of the drawer. From the above stated cases it is clear that in a case where cheque is handed over without filling the name of the payee or other particulars, it is upon accused to prove by positive evidence that he/she did not give implied or express consent to the complainant to fill in the name of the payee and the other particulars. However in the present case no such cogent evidence have been adduced by the accused. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence on record it stands proved that the cheque in question was issued by accused no.2 as director and on behalf of M/s B.T. Distributors. 10. WHETHER THE CHEQUE IN QUESTION HAS BEEN ISSUED IN DISCHARGE OF ANY LEGAL DEBT OR OTHER LIABILITY: It is submitted by the CW­1 that the cheque in question bearing no. 998747 (Ex. CW1/B) dated 21.09.2007 for the sum of Rs. 6,00,000/­ drawn on Syndicate Bank, Scope Minar Complex, Laxmi Nagar, Delhi was issued by accused persons to discharge a liability of Rs.6,00,000/­ towards complainant arisen from a failed sale transaction. As Rs.5,80,000/­ were paid towards principal amount / token money given by the complainant to the accused persons and Rs.20,000/­ was towards interest and compensation for non performance of agreement to sell. At this stage let us go through the relevant provisions of law. There is a presumption in favour of the complainant u/s 118 (a) Negotiable Instruments Act that until the contrary is proved, it will be presumed that every negotiable instrument was drawn for CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 11 of Pages 21 consideration and every such instrument when it has been accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred was accepted, endorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration. Further Section 139 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 provides that it shall be presumed until the contrary is proved that the holder of the cheque received the cheque of the nature referred in the Section 138 for the discharge in whole or in part of his debt or liability. Now it will have to be examined whether the accused has rebutted the presumption as contemplated by Section 118 (b) and Section 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act. It has been observed by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in V.S. Yadav Vs. Reena 172(2010) DLT 561 that the offence u/s 138 NI Act is a technical offence and the complainant is only supposed to prove that the cheques issued by the respondent were dishonored, his statement that cheques were issued against liability or debt is sufficient proof of the debt or liability and the onus shifts to the respondent / accused to show the circumstances under which the cheques came to be issued and this could be proved by the respondent only by way of evidence and not by leading no evidence. It was further observed that in order to rebut the presumption u/s 139 of the NI Act , the accused, by cogent evidence, has to prove the circumstance under which the cheques were issued. It was for the accused to prove if no loan was taken why he did not write a letter to the complainant for return of the cheques. Unless the accused had proved that he acted like a normal businessman / prudent person entering into a contract he could not have rebutted the presumption u/s 139 NI Act. If no loan was given but cheques were retained he immediately would have protested and asked the cheques to be return and still cheques were not returned he would have served a notice as complainant. CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 12 of Pages 21 Similarly in the present case it was for the accused persons to prove why he did not write a letter to the said Mr. Raghvender or the complainant for return of the cheque in question. Unless the accused persons have proved that he acted like a normal businessman / prudent person entering into a transaction he could not have rebutted the presumption u/s 139 NI Act. It was for the accused persons to have protested and asked the complainant or Mr. Raghvender to return the cheque and if still cheque was not returned he would have served a notice as complainant. Therefore after the establishment of the fact that the cheque was issued by the accused and specific statement of the complainant as stated above regarding liability of the accused the burden to rebut the presumption shifted to the accused. It is established principle of law that presumption of law as raised Under sections 138 & 118 of the N.I. Act can be rebutted only by cogent evidence and not by mere plea taken in the statement of the accused recorded under section 313 r.w section 281 of Cr.P.C. Further such cogent evidence can be the cross examination of the complainant or his witnesses (as held in Birender Singh V. state (NCT of Delhi) 2008(1)JCC (NI) 15). In a similar case, Jose Vs. P.C. Joy 2008 (4) RCR (Crl) 251( Kerala HC), it was submitted by the accused that the cheque in question was given by the accused to the complainant as a security. Though the liability was settled as evidenced by Ex. D1 & Ex. D1(a) the cheque was not returned, inspite of requests. Therefore a stop memo was issued to the bank by the accused. He also gave a criminal complaint against the complainant which was taken on file as C.M.P 281/01 ( Ex. D2). On these cogent evidences and the fact of issuing stop memo to the bank and filling a criminal complaint against the complainant the presumption under NI Act stood rebutted. However CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 13 of Pages 21 in the present case there is no cogent evidence whatsoever has been adduced by the accused to support his plea that the cheque in question was given to one Mr. Raghvender. No stop memo has been issued by the accused persons to his bank before presentation and dishonor of the cheque in question. They have not taken any other legal remedy against complainant or Mr. Raghvender. The accused did not called Mr. Raghvender before the court to support the defence plea that the cheque in question was infact given to him for tax purposes. The accused persons have failed to prove this fact from any other document as well that the cheque in question given by them to said Mr. Raghvender. Thus this bald plea of the accused having not been substantiated by any cogent, convincing and clear evidence would not be sufficient to rebut the presumption of law. There is a copy of agreement to sell dated 11.07.2007 on record which is Ex. CW1/A(OSR), which admittedly bears the signature of the complainant and accused no.2, however signatures of accused no. 3 in the same are disputed by the accused no.3. Nonetheless it is admitted fact that this document bears the signature of accused Umesh Wahi. However it is submitted by Ld. Defence Counsel that this document was signed by accused Umesh Wahi in blank condition and was also handed over by him to his accountant Mr. Raghvender for tax purposes, but again apart from this bald plea no cogent evidence have been brought on record to show that this document was given by accused Umesh Wahi to said Mr. Raghvender. This document is in fact an agreement to sell which stats that sum of Rs.3,50,000/­ were handed over by the complainant to accused persons as advance money for the sale of flat bearing no. 33, second floor, Jaipuria Apartment, Kaushambi and the total sale consideration was Rs.25,00,000/­. Further this document also contain a noting on the back of first page which is dated 30.08.2007 whereby the date of execution of sale was extended till 25.09.2007 and a further sum of Rs.2,30,000/­ was CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 14 of Pages 21 received by the accused persons from the complainant. This noting also contain admitted signatures of accused Umesh Wahi and alleged signature of accused Pooja Wahi. This document positively proves the transaction as alleged by the complainant, under which a sum of Rs.5,80,000/­ was handed over by the complainant to the accused persons. However the Ld. Defence Counsel had argued that even if any such agreement to sell was executed between complainant and accused no.2, still that does not entitled the complainant to recover any amount from the accused persons as the said agreement to sell was not registered, hence the transactions became void as the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case entitled Suraj Lamp Industries Pvt Ltd v. State of Haryana has adversely commented on the legality of such documents. The above stated Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court is against the transaction of alleged sales which were done by way of executing an agreement to sell, clubbed with a general power of attorney and will. Hon'ble Supreme Court has no where stated that an agreement to sell should must be registered and otherwise it would became void ab­initio. As per the law contained in registration act 1970 an agreement to sell not coupled with delivery of possession of the immovable property is not required to be registered (as per Section 17(2)(v) of the Registration Act 1970). From the above stated discussion this court is of the opinion that accused no. 2 have failed to prove that document Ex. CW1/A was given by him in blank signed condition to one Mr. Raghvender, on the other hand complainant has been able to prove that this document was executed by accused no.2 Umesh Wahi and might also bear signatures of accused no.3, further the document is a legal document under law. Infact during the cross examination of the complainant a suggestion was given to him that the sale could not be completed due to the lack on the part of the complainant, CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 15 of Pages 21 from this suggestion it appears that even the accused persons accept the execution of such agreement. The presumption U/s 118 & 139 of NI Act are mandatory presumptions in favor of the complainant and the same can not be held to be discharged merely by reason of the fact that the explanation offered by the accused is reasonable and probable. It must further be shown that the explanation is a true one. A fact is said to be proved when its existence is directly established or when upon the material before it Court finds its existence to be so probable that a reasonable man would act on the supposition that it exists. However in the present case the defence put up by the accused persons is not at all probable or reasonable, on the other hand the complainant has proved by positive evidence the liability of the accused persons. The counsel for the accused cited the decision of the Supreme court in his favour titled as Krishna Janardhan Bhat v. Dattataraya G. Hegde (2008) 4 SCC 54, however the ratio of this case that existence of legally recoverable debt is not a matter of presumption under section 139 of the NI Act , has been overruled by the Hon'ble Supreme Court itself in Rangappa Vs Mohan 2010­ TLPRE­0­300 (A Three Judges Bench Judgement) where in it was held: We are in agreement with the respondent­claimant that the presumption mandated by Section 139 of the Act does indeed include the existence of a legally enforceable debt or liability. To that extent, the impugned observations in Krishna Janardhan Bhat (supra) may not be correct. Thus from the above stated discussion it is clear that the accused has failed to rebut the presumptions U/s 118 (b) and 139 of Negotiable Instruments Act . Considering the entire evidence on record, it stands duly CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 16 of Pages 21 proved that the cheques in question which is CW1/B was issued and drawn in discharge of legal liability of the accused and for consideration. 11. WHETHER THE CHEQUE WAS PRESENTED WITHIN THE PERIOD OF VALIDITY: Perusal of the record reveals that the cheque in question which is Ex. CW1/B is dated 21.09.2007, was got dishonoured vide cheque returning memo which is Ex. CW1/C dated 21.09.2007 which clearly shows that the cheque has been presented within period of its validity i.e. within six months from the date of the cheque. Thus this fact stand proved beyond reasonable doubt that cheque was presented for encashment within time. 12. DISHONOUR OF CHEQUE IN QUESTION: In this case CW­1 has got exhibited the cheque returning memo as per section 146 of N.I. Act which is Ex. CW1/C, as per which the cheque in question was dishonoured on the ground of "Insufficient Funds". Ld. Defence Counsel have submitted that in the present matter the cheque was not dishonored for the insufficiency of funds. As on presentation on 21.09.2007, firstly the cheque was honoured at 13:07 pm and later on at 15:53 pm reverse entry was made and the cheque became dishonored, however, at that time there was sufficient balance in the account of the accused. As the account had an overdraft account having overdraft limits of Rs. 1,25,00,000/­(one crore twenty five lacs) and at 15:53 pm there was overdraft of only Rs. ­75,83,391/­ which was much short of the maximum overdraft limit of Rupees.1.25 crore. Hence the cheque was not dishonored due to insufficiency of funds, thus the case U/s 138 NI Act is not made out against the accused persons. On the other hand it is submitted on behalf of the complainant that the dishonor memo is on record and the bank CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 17 of Pages 21 officials have deposed before the court that this dishonor memo was issued by the bank. It is further argued that the relevant point of time is that when the cheque was presented for encashment and at that time the account had already crossed its overdraft limit, that is why after encashing the cheque a reverse entry was made and it was subsequently dishonored. It is further argued by the Ld. Counsel for the complainant that the complainant would not have been benefited to get the cheque dishonored in connivance with the bank officials as for filling a case U/s 138 NI Act he had to sent a legal notice to the accused for the payment of cheque amount only. A number of bank witnesses were examined by the complainant, all of them have submitted that the cheque in question was dishonored as the funds in the overdraft account of the accused persons were not sufficient. However they have pointed certain technicalities of the banking procedure as well but one thing have been stated by all of them that dishonor of the cheque was not a mistake rather its encashment at the first place was a mistake. It is submitted by CW­3 Sh. S.K. Vimal that earlier he encahsed the cheque as he has received information that some funds were going to be deposited in the account of M/s B.T. Distributors, however, later on he received instructions to reverse the entry as the account was going under closure process. It is submitted by the bank official that an overdraft account is closed only when the client have paid the entire overdraft amount. This witness categorically denied the suggestion of the defence counsel that when the cheque was dishonored there was sufficient amount in the account of the accused. Further CW­6 Sh. R.C. Laloria, Branch manager, Laxmi Nagar branch have also deposed that on 21.09.2007 the account of the accused was under the process of closing and relevant entries were being made into that account, at that time it was found that overdraft limit of the accused have been exceeded and on enquiry it was found that the entry pertain to Nirman Vihar branch and CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 18 of Pages 21 consequently we informed that account is under closure process thus they were not supposed to make the entry of Rs.6,00,000/­. Consequently that entry reversed by Nirman Vihar branch. Thus the testimony of both the above witnesses have corroborated each other and they have also explained the entire events of that day. However Ld. defence counsel have pointed out certain contradictions and lapse in procedure adopted by the bank officials eg. Why the bank officials did not wait for the receipt of funds before encashing the cheque, why the bank official did not put his initials after verifying the signatures of the accused and why they had not put the bank's stamp on the cheque at the time of clearance. All these contentions are very technical and not significant for the present case. As the thing to be considered is that the complainant have not got the money and the cheque was ultimately dishonored. Further it was the complainant who had promptly written a letter dated 22.09.2007 (which is on record and admitted by the parties) to the bank officials, complaining them that the cheque in question was earlier encashed and subsequently a reverse entry was made by the bank officials and this reverse entry was made without his approval. This communication clearly shows the bonafide on the part of the complainant. On the other hand the accused who was informed on the very same day i.e. 21.09.2007 by bank manager R.C. Laloria himself that such and such cheque had been deposited in his account and such and such events have taken place despite that the accused never bothered to write any letter to the complainant or to take any legal action against him, infact he did not even replied the legal notice sent by the complainant, this conduct of the accused clearly shows that he was at fault. From the above stated discussion this court is of the considered opinion that the cheque in question was dishonoured on 21.09.2007 with the reason funds insufficient. For the sake of CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 19 of Pages 21 argument even if it is to be said that the cheque was dishonored due to account was under closure even then the accused can not escape his liability U/s 138 NI Act . Further even if there was any alleged fault on the part of bank officials, it is not the complainant who is to suffer because of that. Hence it is proved that the cheque was dishonored due to insufficiency of funds. 13. SERVICE OF LEGAL NOTICE OF DEMAND UPON THE ACCUSED: CW1 has specifically stated in his examination in chief that the complainant got issued the legal notice of demand dated 01.10.2007 which is Ex. CW1/D1 and it was sent to the accused on the same day (within 30 days of knowledge of dishonour of cheque) vide Registered Post and UPC which are Ex. CW1/D2 to Ex. CW1/D4 & Ex. CW1/D5. Returned AD in this regard are Ex. CW1/D6 & Ex. CW1/D7. The legal notice was sent to the accused Umesh Wahi as director of M/s B.T. Distributors at A­61, Swasthya Vihar Delhi, godown no. 81 Basement, Chitra Vihar, Delhi & 532, Gaur Green, Indirapuram, Ghaziabad (U.P.). The accused persons have submitted in their statement recorded U/s 313 Cr. PC that they did not received the legal notice. This court have already observed that no separate notice was issued to accused Pooja Wahi, hence she deserves acquittal on that technical ground only. However with respect to accused Umesh Wahi, managing Director & Authorized signatory of accused no. 1 M/s B.T. Distributors, it is observed that the address mentioned on the postal receipts and legal notice is the same as mentioned by the accused in his personal bond, surety bond & Vakalatnama of Ld. Defence Counsel. Further the Votor I­card filed by Sarla Devi Wahi, W/o Jagan Nath Wahi appears to be mother of the accused Umesh Wahi states her address as A­61, Swasthya Vihar, Delhi. This is CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 20 of Pages 21 the same address which is mentioned on statement of account of the M/s B.T. Distributors Ex. CW4/A as address of the accused no. 1 M/s B.T. Distributors. Thus it stand proved that the notices were sent at the correct address of the accused Umesh Wahi & M/s B.T. Distributors. In K.Bhaskaran v. Sankaran Vaidhyan Balan AIR 1999 SC 3762, it was held by the Apex court that: "No doubt Section 138 of the Act require that the notice should be given only by "post". Nonetheless the principle incorporated in Section 27 (quoted above) can be profitably be imported in a case whee the sender has dispatched the notice by post with the correct address written on it then can be deemed to have been served on the sendee unless he proves that it was not really served and that he was not responsible for such non service. Any other interpretation can lead to a very tenuous position, as the drawer of the cheque who is liable to pay the amount would resort to the strategy of subterfuge by successfully avoiding the notice". The above stated position was again reiterated by the Apex court in C.C. Alavi Haji v. Palapetty Muhammed 's case where apex court further held: It is also to be borne in mind that the requirement of giving of notice is a clear departure from the rule of Criminal Law, where there is no stipulation of giving of a notice before filing a complaint. Any drawer who claims that he did not receive the notice sent by post, can, within 15 days of receipt of summons from the court in respect of the complaint under Section 138 of the Act, make payment of the cheque amount and submit to the Court that he had made payment within 15 days of receipt of summons (by receiving a copy of complaint with the summons) and, therefore, the complaint is liable to be rejected. A person who does not pay within 15 days of receipt of the summons from the Court along with the copy of the complaint under Section 138 of the Act, cannot obviously contend that there CC No.6944/10 ANIL KUMAR JAIN v. B.T. DISTRIBUTORS PVT LTD & OTRS Page no. 21 of Pages 21 was no proper service of notice as required under Section 138 , by ignoring statutory presumption to the contrary under Section 27 of the G.C. Act and Section 114 of the Evidence Act. In the present case the legal notice was dispatched at the correct address of the accused persons, therefore it can be safely deemed that legal notice was duly served upon the accused. 14. THE DRAWER OF THE CHEQUE HAS FAILED TO MAKE THE PAYMENT WITHIN 15 DAYS OF THE RECEIPT OF SAID NOTICE: CW­1 has deposed in his examination in chief that despite service of legal notice of demand accused has failed to pay the cheque amount to the complainant. Accused persons have submitted in their statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C that they did not received the legal notice and there was no question of making any payment to the complainant in respect of the cheque in question as he was not legally liable to pay in respect of the cheque in question. Therefore this fact also stands proved. 15. In view of the aforesaid discussion, I am of the considered opinion that the complainant has proved his case in respect of cheque bearing no. 998747 against the accused company and accused no. 2 Umesh Wahi beyond shadow of reasonable doubts. All the ingredients of Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act have been duly proved on record. Accordingly, accused Umesh Wahi, Director of M/s B.T. Distributors Pvt Ltd S/o Late Sh. J.N. Wahi, R/o A­205, Jaipuria, Indrapuram, Ghaziabad (U.P.) & M/s B.T. Distributors Pvt Ltd stands convicted for the offence U/s 138 read with 141 of Negotiable Instruments Act . Accused no. 3 Pooja Wahi have been acquitted as legal notice was not issued to her. Let free copy be supplied to Umesh Wahi.
